Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may be affecting your well-being. The purpose of this assessment is to get a better understanding of your emotional experience in the postpartum period, so we can provide you with the best possible support and care.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and held in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and help, not to judge. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your feelings and experiences over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and natural as possible.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling overwhelmed, anxious, or sad?

Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. Taking care of the baby is exhausting, and some days I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I used to love reading and taking long walks, but lately, I haven't had the energy or interest in doing those things. I've been feeling anxious about the baby's health and safety, and it's hard for me to shake off those worries. Sometimes I feel like I'm not doing enough or that I'm not a good enough mother, which makes me feel guilty and inadequate. 

I do have moments where I feel okay, like when the baby smiles at me or when my partner helps out, but overall, I've been feeling really sad and discouraged. I cry a few times a week, usually when I'm stressed or feeling overwhelmed. It's like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying my life or my new role as a mother. I'm hoping that talking to you will help me figure out why I'm feeling this way and how I can start feeling better.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, I haven't been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as I used to. I mean, sometimes my partner will make a joke or something will happen with the baby that's cute, and I'll smile or even laugh for a second, but it's not the same as it used to be. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. 

It's hard to explain, but even when I do laugh, it feels kind of forced or superficial. Like, I'm laughing on the outside, but on the inside, I'm still feeling anxious or sad. It's like I'm just going through the motions of being happy, but I'm not really feeling it. And that's hard for me, because I used to be a pretty happy and carefree person, and now I just feel like I'm struggling to find joy in things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

That's something I've really been struggling with lately. I haven't been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll have a plan to do something, like meet a friend for coffee or go for a walk, and I'll just feel really meh about it. I won't really be excited or looking forward to it like I would have before the baby was born. 

Even things that I used to love, like reading or trying out a new restaurant, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I'll think about doing something fun, but then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do for the baby, or I'll worry about how I'll manage to take care of her while I'm trying to do something for myself. It's like my mind is just consumed by all these responsibilities and worries, and I don't have the energy or motivation to look forward to things like I used to. 

Sometimes I'll think about how I used to look forward to the weekends, or a night out with my partner, and now those things just seem like a distant memory. It's hard for me to imagine feeling carefree and excited about things again, but at the same time, I really want to get back to that place. I just don't know how to get there right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is fussy, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If my partner is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting them enough. It's like I'm always looking for ways to criticize myself and feel guilty about something. 

And it's not just the big things. I'll blame myself for little things too, like if I forget to wash a bottle or if I run out of diapers. I'll think to myself, "How could you be so forgetful? You're a terrible mother." It's like I'm always expecting myself to be perfect, and when I'm not, I feel like I've failed somehow. 

It's hard for me to shake off those feelings of guilt and self-blame. I know it's not rational, but it's just how I feel. And it's exhausting, because I'm always beating myself up over something. I wish I could be kinder to myself and just acknowledge that I'm doing the best I can, but it's hard for me to do that right now.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something. Like, what if she gets sick? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if I'm not doing everything I can to keep her safe? It's like my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel so anxious and on edge. 

And the thing is, there's no real reason for me to be worried. The baby is healthy, she's gaining weight, she's hitting all her milestones. But my mind just can't seem to shut off, and I'll find myself lying awake at night, thinking about all the things that could go wrong. It's like I'm constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? 

Sometimes I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sense of anxiety. My heart will start racing, my palms will get sweaty, and I'll just feel like I'm going to panic. It's really scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I'll try to calm myself down, but it's hard when my mind is just racing with all these worries and fears. 

It's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and myself at the same time. I'll worry about everything, really. It's like my mind is just constantly looking for things to worry about, and it's exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or watching TV, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my breath will get shallow, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to something, but there's no real reason for it. 

It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening or how to make it stop. I'll try to calm myself down, but it's hard when my mind is racing and my body is feeling so out of control. Sometimes I'll feel like I'm going to lose control completely, and that's a really terrifying feeling. 

One time, I was holding the baby and I just felt this overwhelming sense of panic. I didn't know what was wrong, but I just felt like something was terribly wrong. I started shaking and crying, and my partner had to come over and calm me down. It was really embarrassing, but at the same time, it was just so overwhelming. 

It's not just the panic attacks, either. Sometimes I'll just feel this constant, low-level sense of anxiety. It's like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, or for something bad to happen. And it's exhausting, because I'm always on edge, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. 

I don't know how to make it stop, or how to calm myself down when it happens. That's one of the things I'm hoping to work on with you - learning how to manage these feelings of panic and anxiety, and finding ways to calm myself down when I'm feeling overwhelmed.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly running on a treadmill and getting nowhere. I'm tired all the time, but I never seem to get a break. 

And it's not just the physical exhaustion. It's the emotional exhaustion too. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about the baby, and about being a good mother, and about keeping everything together. It's like I'm shouldering this huge responsibility, and it's weighing me down. 

Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. Like, I'll be doing okay, and then something will happen - the baby will cry, or I'll spill something, or I'll realize I've forgotten to do something important - and it's like the whole house of cards comes crashing down. I'll just feel overwhelmed and like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities and worries. 

I feel like I'm not doing anything well, either. I'm not a good enough mother, I'm not a good enough partner, I'm not a good enough person. It's like I'm constantly falling short, and that's a really hard feeling to live with. 

It's hard for me to ask for help, too. I feel like I should be able to do everything on my own, and that asking for help is a sign of weakness. But at the same time, I know that I need help. I need someone to talk to, someone to support me, someone to help me figure out how to get through this really tough time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. It's because my mind is racing and I'm feeling so overwhelmed and unhappy. I'll lie in bed and just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, like I'm never going to be happy again. 

I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, like the baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just feeling like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mother. And it's hard to turn those thoughts off, you know? It's like my brain is just constantly going, going, going, and I don't know how to make it stop. 

Sometimes I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night and just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness. It's like I'm grieving the life I had before the baby, or the person I used to be. I know that's not rational, but it's just how I feel. 

And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem. It's the fact that I'm not sleeping because I'm unhappy, and that's just making everything worse. I feel like I'm trapped in this cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free. 

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. They just tell me to try to relax, or to take a warm bath, or to practice deep breathing. And I know those things can help, but they're not getting at the root of the problem. The problem is that I'm just really struggling to be happy right now, and I don't know how to fix that.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me for a while now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but inside, I'm feeling really sad and miserable. It's like I'm living in a fog, and I don't know how to escape it. 

I'll have moments where I'll be holding the baby, or looking at her, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll start crying, and I won't be able to stop. It's like my emotions are just right at the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. 

I feel like I've lost myself in all of this. I used to be a happy person, I used to enjoy things, but now it's just like I'm trudging through every day. I don't feel like me anymore. I feel like I'm just a shadow of my former self, and it's really hard to deal with. 

I'll try to put on a happy face for my partner, or for our families, but it's hard to keep that up. Sometimes I'll just break down and cry, and it's like I'm saying, "I don't know if I can do this anymore." 

It's not just the baby, it's not just being a new mom. It's like everything is just feeling really overwhelming, and I don't know how to cope. I feel like I'm just barely holding on, and it's scary. 

I'm worried that I'm not bonding with the baby the way I should be. I'm worried that I'm not being a good enough mom. I'm worried that I'm just not cut out for this. And all of those worries just make me feel even more sad and miserable. 

I just wish I could feel happy again. I wish I could feel like myself again. I wish I could just enjoy this time with my baby, without all of these feelings of sadness and anxiety weighing me down.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. I'll be changing the baby's diaper, or feeding her, or just sitting there holding her, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming wave of emotion, and I'll start crying. 

It's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be with my partner, or with our families, and I'll just start crying. It's embarrassing, but I just can't help it. It's like all of these emotions are just bottled up inside of me, and they need to come out somehow. 

I've cried in front of my partner, and it's hard for them to see me like that. They'll try to comfort me, and tell me everything is okay, but it's hard for them to understand what I'm going through. They'll say things like, "You're a great mom," or "You're doing a great job," but it's hard for me to believe that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and sad. 

I've even cried in front of the baby, which is hard for me. I don't want her to see me like that, but sometimes I just can't help it. I'll be holding her, and I'll just start crying, and she'll look up at me with these big, round eyes, and it's like she's trying to understand what's wrong with me. 

It's hard for me to explain why I'm crying, too. Sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so overwhelmed, and sometimes it's because I'm feeling so sad and miserable. But sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so guilty, like I'm not doing enough for the baby, or like I'm not being a good enough mom. 

I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just be happy, and enjoy this time with my baby, without all of these emotions weighing me down. But it's hard, because it feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to deal with it all.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
